The Big Story · Economy

Japan’s price number fell. The pressure did not.

Wholesale inflation slowed to 6.8% in September and missed forecasts. Then one line in the Bank of Japan’s table changed the picture: nonferrous metals were 40.2% more expensive than a year earlier.

Culture · Opens tomorrow

A Kyoto gate became a death sentence. Tomorrow, its hidden world opens in Tokyo.

Daitokuji’s 700-year exhibition gathers 14 National Treasures, 69 Important Cultural Properties and normally unseen statues from the gate linked to Sen no Rikyū.

Prices

A lower rate is not a lower price

September’s 6.8% annual CGPI rise means business goods remained costlier than a year earlier; the 0.3% monthly fall measures a different comparison.

The Brief

08:50

BOJ releases September corporate prices

Domestic goods +6.8% year on year; −0.3% from August. Figures are preliminary.

Daitokuji advance ticket sales end

DATA

Import prices remain elevated

The yen-based import price index rose 24.5% from a year earlier.

Japanese word of the day企業物価 · kigyō bukka

“Corporate goods prices.” 企業 means company; 物価 means the price level. It is an economic-news term for upstream prices, not a shopper’s receipt.

Why today matters

Japan’s wholesale-price headline softened, but imported materials kept sending a different signal. In Tokyo, a 700-year-old Zen network prepares to reveal objects rarely seen together. One day, two forms of pressure: the costs moving through modern supply chains, and the power preserved inside historic art.
